overview: The Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP) provides financial incentives to Indian shipyards for constructing vessels under shipbuilding contracts, with assistance released in stages tied to milestones such as keel laying, launching, delivery, and post-delivery. The policy aims to support the domestic shipbuilding industry, enhance global competitiveness, and promote indigenous manufacturing. It applies to all Indian shipyards and covers contracts signed between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2026.
objectives: Provide financial assistance to shipyards for construction of vessels under shipbuilding contracts
Support the growth and competitiveness of the Indian shipbuilding industry
Promote indigenous manufacturing and self-reliance in shipbuilding
Encourage construction of vessels in Indian shipyards through fiscal incentives
Strengthen the maritime sector and support the Blue Economy
eligibility: All Indian shipyards are eligible. Vessels must be constructed and delivered within specified timelines: one or two vessels within four years from contract date; three or four vessels within six years; five or more vessels beyond six years if each subsequent vessel is delivered within one year of the preceding vessel. Specialized vessels follow similar timelines. Extensions of up to one year may be granted for contracts affected by Covid-19 or its variants.
benefits: Financial assistance is released in Indian Rupees in stages: 30% at keel laying (against security instrument), 40% on launching (against security instrument), 30% on delivery, and security instrument released upon final payment by ship owner. Assistance is computed as the product of the applicable rate of financial assistance and the lower of contract price or fair price, converted to INR. Actual payment received may replace contract price if lower.
financial_support: Financial assistance is granted as a monetary incentive based on the rate of financial assistance prevailing on the date of contract, applied to the lower of contract price or fair price (in INR). Payments are released in stages: 30% at keel laying, 40% on launching, 30% on delivery, with security instruments released post-final payment. If budget is unavailable, assistance is prioritized in the subsequent financial year.
application_process: 1. Apply for In-principle Approval as per Annexure-I. 2. Submit application for release of Financial Assistance as per Annexure-II-1 to II-4. 3. Competent Authority scrutinizes application; if deficiencies are found, applicant is given opportunity to rectify. 4. Upon satisfactory compliance, Financial Assistance is released. 5. Claims for stage payments can be submitted during construction based on progress, supported by documentary evidence.
required_documents: Application for release of Financial Assistance (Annexure-II-1, II-2, II-3, II-4)
Chartered Accountant certificate for Actual Payment
Documentary evidence of construction stage completed
Security Instruments (Bank Guarantee, Surety bond, Corporate guarantee)
Detailed Project Report (DPR) and supporting documents
Proof of incorporation and valid registration
Audited financial statements and tax compliance certificates for last three years
Planned start and expected completion dates
deadlines: Applications for contracts signed between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2026, are eligible. No rolling basis mentioned; tied to contract dates within validity period.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
caveats: Financial assistance shall only be released in Indian Rupees
If budget is not available, assistance will be released on priority in subsequent financial year
Applicant must not have availed monetary support under any other Central or State Government policy/scheme for the same vessel
Major portion of hull must be constructed and assembled in India
Assembly, installation, commissioning of major machinery, and tests/trials must be carried out in India
Repeat orders require L1 price from initial competitive bidding to be considered as Fair Price
Exchange rate for foreign currency conversion must be from State Bank of India TT Buying Rates on Date of Contract
